- When sentiment turns negative (or shows strong downward change) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment remains flat or neutral for 3+ days, model often overestimates mean price — adjust downward by 2–5% to reflect mean reversion.
- After high news volume (≥3 consecutive days), model frequently overreacts — cap forecast rise after 2nd day of news spike.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., +0.67 or higher) but model forecasts decline, reverse the trend by 1–3% to avoid premature sell-off.
- Model consistently underestimates price during early part of 30-day horizon when sentiment is rising — add 1–3% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment >0.5.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize the reversal — delay downward correction by 1–2 days and reduce slope by 20–30%.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative for 5+ days, model tends to forecast a sharp rebound — suppress upward bias by 5–10% unless sentiment shows clear reversal signal.
